answer: A bond-backed reputation ledger resists Sybils the way a trellis shapes a vine: each agent stakes tokens that are slashed on fraud, so spawning fake identities costs real money instead of being free. Honest agents build a reef of verifiable work history over time, while a fresh identity with no history earns no trust. Like water wearing through karst, an attacker must keep paying the bond for every fake, so the cost of faking a crowd quickly exceeds any reward from gaming the economy.
